name: Belep
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source.
catalog_citation: McCracken, Chelsea Leigh. 2012. A grammar of Belep. PhD dissertation, Rice University (repository.rice.edu, hdl 1911/71287).
catalog_quote: Phonological words in Belep receive stress. According to the typology of stress systems described by Van Zanten & Goedemans (2007), Belep has primarily fixed stress on the penultimate syllable. This is complicated by a large amount of extrametricality of formatives, and by some degree of lexical stress. Furthermore, the traditional cross-linguistic correlates of stress—vowel duration, intensity, and pitch (Lehiste 1970)—behave independently in Belep, making stress difficult to identify in many cases, both instrumentally and to native speaker judgments. ... In disyllabic words, the penultimate syllable is stressed—it contains a vowel of longer duration (§2.3.2.1) and the word’s intensity peak—while the final syllable is unstressed and contains the pitch peak. ... Speakers do not consistently identify stress in trisyllabic words. ... For phonological reasons, I will consider the penultima…

audit.reasoning: Quote confirmed verbatim at the stated sections/pages in the Rice PDF we hold/text. The deciding source is the sole and authoritative description of Belep (modern fieldwork reference grammar with an explicit, argued prosody section including phonetic correlates); Glottolog lists only this work (three issues) and web search finds no other stress/prosody study. Coding (penultimate fixed stress on the phonological word, most clitics/suffixes extrametrical, possessive/determiner/specific suffixes counted, small listed set of initial-stress lexical exceptions) matches 2.7.3-2.7.5 as read. Only works still to obtain is the paywalled 2019 MGL edition of the same grammar, low priority. Nothing open to download, so nothing
